discoveries.title: The Collins–Shor peak location holds for every tree of order 21, 22 and 23
discoveries.statement: For a tree T of order n, D(T) is its distance matrix, δ_k(T) is the coefficient of x^k in det(D(T) − xI), and d_k(T) = 2^{k−(n−2)} |δ_k(T)| for 0 ≤ k ≤ n − 2 are the normalized coefficients of the distance characteristic polynomial. For every tree T of order n with 3 ≤ n ≤ 23, every index k at which d_0(T), …, d_{n−2}(T) attains its maximum satisfies ⌊n/2⌋ ≤ k ≤ ⌈n − n/√5⌉. The range 3 ≤ n ≤ 20 (1,346,022 trees) reproduces the verification reported in arXiv:1507.02341; the range 21 ≤ n ≤ 23 (22,596,335 trees) is the contribution.

discoveries.title: Laplacian formula for the normalized distance characteristic polynomial of a tree
discoveries.statement: Let T be a tree of order n ≥ 3 with distance matrix D and Laplacian matrix L, and let τ be the vector with entries τ_v = 2 − deg(v). Then, as polynomials in x, −2^{−(n−2)} det(2xI − D) = (n − 1) det(I + xL) − x τᵀ adj(I + xL) τ.

discoveries.title: Distance characteristic polynomial of a caterpillar through a quotient matrix
discoveries.statement: Let T be a caterpillar of order n whose spine v_1, …, v_s is a path and whose spine vertex v_i carries c_i ≥ 1 pendant leaves, so that n = s + c_1 + … + c_s, and let D be its distance matrix. Let Q be the 2s × 2s matrix indexed by the s spine vertices and the s classes of leaves, with entries, for 1 ≤ i, j ≤ s: from spine vertex i to spine vertex j, |i − j|; from spine vertex i to leaf class j, (|i − j| + 1) c_j; from leaf class i to spine vertex j, |i − j| + 1; from leaf class i to leaf class j, (|i − j| + 2) c_j if i ≠ j and 2(c_i − 1) if i = j. Then det(xI − D) = (x + 2)^{n−2s} det(xI − Q).

discoveries.title: The star does not minimize the coefficient ratios up to the middle index: the double star S(9,9)
discoveries.statement: For a tree T of order n, D(T) is its distance matrix, δ_k(T) is the coefficient of x^k in det(D(T) − xI), and d_k(T) = 2^{k−(n−2)} |δ_k(T)| for 0 ≤ k ≤ n − 2 are the normalized coefficients of the distance characteristic polynomial. Let ρ_k(T) = d_{k+1}(T)/d_k(T), and let S_n be the star of order n. The statement 'ρ_k(T) ≥ ρ_k(S_n) for every tree T of order n and every 0 ≤ k ≤ ⌊n/2⌋ − 1' is false. It fails at n = 20 and k = 9 for the double star S(9,9) (two adjacent vertices, each with 9 pendant leaves): the quotient d_9/d_10 equals 10255/10791 for S(9,9) and 94/99 for S_20, and 10255/10791 > 94/99, hence ρ_9(S(9,9)) < ρ_9(S_20).

discoveries.title: The path maximizes the coefficient ratios up to its own peak
discoveries.statement: For a tree T of order n, D(T) is its distance matrix, δ_k(T) is the coefficient of x^k in det(D(T) − xI), and d_k(T) = 2^{k−(n−2)} |δ_k(T)| for 0 ≤ k ≤ n − 2 are the normalized coefficients of the distance characteristic polynomial. Let ρ_k(T) = d_{k+1}(T)/d_k(T) for 0 ≤ k ≤ n − 3, let P_n be the path of order n, and let p_n be the largest index at which d_0(P_n), …, d_{n−2}(P_n) attains its maximum. discoveries.title: The peak of the normalized distance coefficients of every double star is at ⌊n/2⌋
discoveries.statement: For a tree T of order n, D(T) is its distance matrix, δ_k(T) is the coefficient of x^k in det(D(T) − xI), and d_k(T) = 2^{k−(n−2)} |δ_k(T)| for 0 ≤ k ≤ n − 2 are the normalized coefficients of the distance characteristic polynomial. For integers a, b ≥ 1 let S(a,b) be the double star: two adjacent vertices carrying a and b pendant leaves, of order n = a + b + 2, and let m = ⌊n/2⌋. Then d_{m−1}(S(a,b)) < d_m(S(a,b)), and d_{m+1}(S(a,b)) < d_m(S(a,b)) whenever m + 1 ≤ n − 2. Consequently m is the only index at which d_0(S(a,b)), …, d_{n−2}(S(a,b)) attains its maximum, and since ⌊n/2⌋ ≤ ⌈n − n/√5⌉, Conjecture 1.2 of arXiv:1507.02341 (Collins–Shor) holds for every double star, that is, for every tree of diameter 3.

discoveries.title: The peak of the normalized distance coefficients of the caterpillar K(a,0,c), a, c ≥ 1, a + c ≥ 3, is at ⌊n/2⌋
discoveries.statement: For a tree T of order n, D(T) is its distance matrix, δ_k(T) is the coefficient of x^k in det(D(T) − xI), and d_k(T) = 2^{k−(n−2)} |δ_k(T)| for 0 ≤ k ≤ n − 2 are the normalized coefficients of the distance characteristic polynomial. For integers a, c ≥ 1 with a + c ≥ 3 let K(a,0,c) be the tree with a path v_1 v_2 v_3 in which v_1 carries a pendant leaves, v_3 carries c pendant leaves and v_2 none; its order is n = a + c + 3 ≥ 6. Let m = ⌊n/2⌋. Then d_{m−1}(K(a,0,c)) < d_m(K(a,0,c)) and d_{m+1}(K(a,0,c)) < d_m(K(a,0,c)). Consequently m is the only index at which d_0(K(a,0,c)), …, d_{n−2}(K(a,0,c)) attains its maximum, and since ⌊n/2⌋ ≤ ⌈n − n/√5⌉, Conjecture 1.2 of arXiv:1507.02341 (Collins–Shor) holds for K(a,0,c).

discoveries.title: Hypothesis V: the mixed second partials of d_m − d_{m−1} are non-negative for caterpillars with any number of spine vertices
discoveries.statement: Let s ≥ 2 be an integer and c = (c_1, …, c_s) real variables. Let Q(c) be the 2s × 2s matrix with blocks, for 1 ≤ i, j ≤ s: |i − j| (rows 1 to s, columns 1 to s); (|i − j| + 1) c_j (rows 1 to s, columns s + 1 to 2s); |i − j| + 1 (rows s + 1 to 2s, columns 1 to s); and, for rows s + 1 to 2s and columns s + 1 to 2s, (|i − j| + 2) c_j if i ≠ j and 2(c_i − 1) if i = j. Define the polynomials g_0(c), …, g_{2s}(c) by −det(2xI − Q(c)) / 4^{s−1} = Σ_{j=0}^{2s} g_j(c) x^j. For an integer n ≥ 2s let m = ⌊n/2⌋ and D_n(c) = Σ_{j=0}^{2s} g_j(c) [C(n − 2s, m − j) − C(n − 2s, m − 1 − j)], where C(N, i) is the binomial coefficient, equal to 0 when i < 0 or i > N. Hypothesis V: for every s ≥ 2, every integer n ≥ 2s and all 1 ≤ i < k ≤ s, the mixed partial derivative ∂²D_n/∂c_i∂c_k is non-negative at every real point c with c_1 ≥ 1, c_s ≥ 1 and c_j ≥ 0 for 1 < j < s. (On the points c with non-negative integer coordinates and c_1 + … + c_s = n − s, D_n(c) is d_m − d_{m−1} for the caterpillar with spine v_1 … v_s and c_i pendant leaves at v_i.)

discoveries.title: Conjecture Γ: a non-negative half-gamma expansion for the coefficient polynomials of a tree with pendant leaves
discoveries.statement: Let S be a tree on s ≥ 2 vertices with vertex set V and distance matrix P, let J be the all-ones s × s matrix and 1 the all-ones vector. For A ⊆ V let a = |A|, let 1_A be the indicator vector of A, and let I_{V∖A} be the diagonal matrix whose diagonal is the indicator vector of V ∖ A. Put, for x ≠ 0, N_A(x) = 2x I_{V∖A} − P − 1_A 1ᵀ − 1 1_Aᵀ − (a/(2x)) J and r_A(x) = −2^{2−s} · x · det N_A(x), which is a polynomial in x of degree at most d = s − a + 1. Conjecture Γ: for every tree S on at least two vertices and every A ⊆ V with |A| ≥ 2, there are real numbers ρ_e ≥ 0 (for integers e ≥ 0 with 2e < d) and σ_e ≥ 0 (for integers e with d ≤ 2e ≤ 2d) such that r_A(x) = Σ_{2e<d} ρ_e x^e (1+x)^{d−2e} + Σ_{d≤2e≤2d} σ_e x^e.

discoveries.title: The polynomials r_A of a tree depend only on a Laplacian block; non-negative half-gamma expansion when the complement of A is independent or has at most two vertices
discoveries.statement: Let S be a tree on s ≥ 2 vertices with vertex set V, distance matrix P and Laplacian L; g_v is the degree of v in S, J the all-ones s × s matrix and 1 the all-ones vector. For A ⊆ V let a = |A|, B = V ∖ A, t = |B|, 1_A the indicator vector of A, I_B the diagonal matrix whose diagonal is the indicator vector of B, and, for x ≠ 0, N_A(x) = 2x I_B − P − 1_A 1ᵀ − 1 1_Aᵀ − (a/(2x)) J and r_A(x) = −2^{2−s} · x · det N_A(x), a polynomial of degree at most t + 1. Let L_B = L[B, B], Φ_B(x) = det(I + x L_B), h_w = g_w − 1 and H = Σ_{w∈B} h_w, k_w the number of neighbours of w that lie in B, e_B the number of edges of S with both ends in B, and z the vector (2h_w − k_w)_{w∈B}. For an integer d ≥ 0, a polynomial has a non-negative half-gamma expansion of degree d if it equals Σ_{e≥0, 2e<d} ρ_e x^e (1+x)^{d−2e} + Σ_{d≤2e≤2d} σ_e x^e with all ρ_e ≥ 0 and σ_e ≥ 0. (i) r_A(x) = Φ_B(x) · [a(1+x) + (3 + 3H − 2e_B) x] − x² · zᵀ adj(I + x L_B) z; in particular r_A is determined by s and by the matrix L_B up to a simultaneous permutation of its rows and columns. (ii) Every non-negative combination of polynomials x^e (1+x)^j with integers e, j ≥ 0, e + j ≤ d and 2e + j ≥ d has a non-negative half-gamma expansion of degree d. (iii) If B is non-empty and no two vertices of B are adjacent in S, then a − H ≥ 1, r_A(x) = (a − H)(1+x) Φ_B + 3x Φ_B + Σ_{w∈B} [h_w (1+x)² + 3 h_w x(1+x) + h_w² x] Φ_w with Φ_B = Π_{w∈B} (1 + g_w x) and Φ_w = Π_{u∈B, u≠w} (1 + g_u x), and r_A has a non-negative half-gamma expansion of degree t + 1. (iv) If B = {w} and g = g_w, then r_A(x) = (s−1)(1+x)² + [(g−1)s + 2g + 1] x + [(g−1)(s+6−g) + 3] x², with the three coefficients positive. (v) If s ≥ 3 and B = {u, w} with u ≠ w, Σ = g_u + g_w, Π = g_u g_w, and ε = 1 if u and w are adjacent and ε = 0 otherwise, then r_A(x) = (s−2)(1+x)³ + ρ_1 x(1+x) + σ_2 x² + σ_3 x³ with ρ_1 = (s+1)Σ − 2s + 1 − 2ε, σ_2 = (s+6)(Π − ε) − Σ² + (2+2ε)Σ − s − 3, σ_3 = (s+11−2ε)Π − ΣΠ − 4(1−ε)Σ − (s+11)ε − s + 2, and ρ_1 ≥ 3, σ_2 ≥ 3, σ_3 ≥ 3.

discoveries.statement: For an integer d ≥ 0 let C_d be the set of non-negative combinations of the polynomials x^e (1+x)^i with integers e, i ≥ 0, e + i ≤ d and 2e + i ≥ d. (i) For every tree T on j ≥ 1 vertices with Laplacian L_T and every function ν from the vertices of T to the non-negative integers that is not identically zero, det(I + x (L_T + diag(ν))) ∈ C_j. (ii) Let S be a tree on s ≥ 2 vertices with vertex set V and Laplacian L, g_v the degree of v, A ⊆ V with 1 ≤ |A| ≤ s − 1, a = |A|, B = V ∖ A, t = |B|, L_B = L[B, B], Φ_B(x) = det(I + x L_B), H = Σ_{w∈B} (g_w − 1) and e_B the number of edges of S with both ends in B. Then Φ_B ∈ C_t, 3 + 3H − 2e_B ≥ 3 and Φ_B · [a(1+x) + (3 + 3H − 2e_B) x] ∈ C_{t+1}. (iii) With S and A as in (ii), let r_A^S be the polynomial r_A of MD-0011 for the tree S, let S′ be the graph obtained from S by contracting each connected component of the subgraph induced by A to a single vertex, and let A′ be the set of the a′ contracted vertices. Consequently, if r_{A′}^{S′} has a non-negative half-gamma expansion of degree t + 1 (as defined in MD-0011), then so has r_A^S.

discoveries.title: The polynomials r_A have only real negative roots; third form and leading coefficient
discoveries.statement: Let S be a tree on s ≥ 2 vertices with vertex set V, Laplacian L and degrees g_v, τ_v = 2 − g_v, A ⊆ V with 1 ≤ |A| ≤ s − 1, B = V ∖ A, t = |B|, L_B = L[B, B], Φ_B(x) = det(I + x L_B), p the vector indexed by B with entries 1 + τ_w x, τ_B the restriction of τ to B, and r_A the polynomial of MD-0011. (i) r_A(x) = (s + (s + 3)x) Φ_B(x) − pᵀ adj(I + x L_B) p. (ii) L_B is positive definite; r_A has degree exactly t + 1 and leading coefficient κ · det L_B, where κ = s + 3 − τ_Bᵀ L_B^{−1} τ_B; and κ ≥ 4, with equality if and only if |A| = 1. (iii) All t + 1 roots of r_A, counted with multiplicity, are real and negative; hence all coefficients of r_A are positive and form a log-concave sequence. (iv) If |A| ≥ 2 and P_A is the distance matrix of S restricted to A, then (κ − 4) · 1ᵀ adj(P_A) 1 = 2 det P_A.

discoveries.statement: For a tree T on j ≥ 1 vertices with Laplacian L_T and degrees k_v, and a function ν from its vertices to the non-negative integers, let N = Σ_v ν_v, M(T, ν) = I + x(L_T + diag ν), Φ(T, ν) = det M(T, ν), p the vector with entries 1 + (2 − k_v − ν_v)x, and R(T, ν) = (N + j − 1)(1 + x) Φ(T, ν) − pᵀ adj(M(T, ν)) p. C_d is the cone of MD-0012; Γ_c is the statement: R(T, ν) ∈ C_{j+1} for every tree T on j ≥ 1 vertices and every ν that is not identically zero. (i) Let S be a tree on s ≥ 2 vertices, A a set of vertices with 1 ≤ |A| ≤ s − 1, B its complement, T_1, …, T_c the components of the subgraph induced by B, ν_w the number of neighbours of w ∈ B in A, e_A the number of edges with both ends in A, Φ_B and r_A as in MD-0012 and MD-0011. Then r_A = [(1 + 4x) + e_A (1 + x)] Φ_B + Σ_i R(T_i, ν) Π_{l ≠ i} Φ(T_l, ν). Consequently, if Γ_c holds, then for every tree S on s ≥ 2 vertices and every non-empty set A of vertices, r_A has a non-negative half-gamma expansion of degree s − |A| + 1 (as defined in MD-0011); in particular Conjecture Γ (MD-0010) holds. (ii) Let j ≥ 2, w a leaf of T with neighbour u and ν_w = 0, T′ = T − w, T_1, …, T_q the components of T′ − u, u_i the neighbour of u in T_i, Φ_i = Φ(T_i, ν + e_{u_i}) and R_i = R(T_i, ν + e_{u_i}). Then R(T, ν) = (1 + x) R(T′, ν) + x [ν_u (1 + x) Π_i Φ_i + Σ_i R_i Π_{l ≠ i} Φ_l]. (iii) For every vertex w of T, with T_1, …, T_q the components of T − w, w_i the neighbour of w in T_i, Φ_i = Φ(T_i, ν + e_{w_i}), R_i = R(T_i, ν + e_{w_i}), Ψ_w = Π_i Φ_i and π_w = e_wᵀ adj(M(T, ν)) p: R(T, ν + e_w) = R(T, ν) + (1 + x) Φ(T, ν) + 2x π_w + [(ν_w + 1) x (1 + x) − x²] Ψ_w + x Σ_i R_i Π_{l ≠ i} Φ_l. (iv) Let j ≥ 2, w a leaf of T with neighbour u, ν⁰ the function ν with ν_w replaced by 0, and E = R(T, ν⁰ + e_w) − R(T, ν⁰). Then R(T, ν) = R(T, ν⁰) + ν_w E + ν_w (ν_w − 1) x Φ(T − w, ν + e_u). (v) Suppose j ≥ 2 and R(T″, μ) ∈ C_{j″+1} for every tree T″ on j″ < j vertices and every μ that is not identically zero. discoveries.title: The Wiener form of the distance polynomial of a tree, and the bound ⌊(n−1)/2⌋ on the peak of its normalized coefficients
discoveries.statement: Let T be a tree of order n ≥ 2 with vertex set V, distance matrix D, Laplacian L, transmissions t_v = Σ_u dist(u, v) and Wiener index W = ½ Σ_v t_v. Put ℓ_T(x) = −2^{−(n−2)} det(2xI − D) and Φ(x) = det(I + xL), and for distinct u, v ∈ V let Π_{uv}(x) = det((I + xL)[Q, Q]), where Q is the set of vertices not on the path from u to v (Π_{uv} = 1 if Q is empty). (i) n² ℓ_T(x) = 4 (W − n x) Φ(x) + Σ_{{u,v}} (t_u − t_v)² x^{dist(u,v)−1} Π_{uv}(x), the sum over the unordered pairs of distinct vertices. (ii) If n ≥ 3, d_k = 2^{k−(n−2)} |δ_k| (0 ≤ k ≤ n − 2) are the normalized coefficients, δ_k being the coefficient of x^k in det(D − xI), and μ = ⌊(n−1)/2⌋, then d_{μ−1} < d_μ; consequently every index at which d_0, …, d_{n−2} attains its maximum is at least ⌊(n−1)/2⌋. In particular, for odd n every such index is at least ⌊n/2⌋.

For every vertex c, with δ_v = dist(c, v): ℓ_T = Σ_{e∈E} Π_e + 4 Σ_{v≠c} δ_v x^{δ_v} Π_{cv} − 4x Π_{{c}} + Σ (δ_u − δ_v)² x^{dist(u,v)−1} Π_{uv}, the last sum over the unordered pairs {u, v} with dist(u, v) ≥ 2. (ii) (Leaf polynomial.) If T⁺ is T with a new pendant vertex attached at c, then ℓ_{T⁺} − (1+x) ℓ_T = (1+4x) Π_{{c}} + x Σ_{e∈E, c∉e} Π_{e∪{c}} + Σ (δ_a − δ_b)² x^{dist(a,b)} Π_{P∪{c}} + Σ_{a: δ_a ≥ 2} (δ_a − 1)² x^{δ_a} Π_{ac}, the third sum over the unordered pairs {a, b} with dist(a, b) ≥ 2 whose path P does not contain c (P its vertex set). In particular Ω_c(T) := ℓ_{T⁺} − (1+x) ℓ_T − (1+4x) Π_{{c}} has non-negative coefficients. (iii) (Remainder.) Put Θ_T = (Φ − (1+x)^{n−1})/x and Ω_T = ℓ_T + 4x(1+x)^{n−1} − (1+4x) Θ_T. For every chain of subtrees T_1 ⊂ … ⊂ T_n = T with |T_k| = k, T_{k+1} being T_k with a pendant vertex attached at u_k: Θ_T = Σ_{k=1}^{n−1} (1+x)^{n−1−k} Π_{{u_k}}(T_k) and Ω_T = Σ_{k=1}^{n−1} (1+x)^{n−1−k} Ω_{u_k}(T_k). Consequently Ω_T has non-negative coefficients. (iv) (Even order.) If n = 2m ≥ 4 and d_k denotes the coefficient of x^k in ℓ_T (the normalized coefficients of the distance characteristic polynomial, 0 ≤ k ≤ n − 2), then d_m − d_{m−1} ≥ (n−1)(3m−5)/(m+1) · C(2m−2, m−1)/m + ([x^m] − [x^{m−1}]) Ω_T, with equality when T is a star, for which Ω_T = 0.

discoveries.title: The lower bound ⌊n/2⌋ for the peak of the normalized coefficients of the distance characteristic polynomial of every tree; star minimality in the half-gamma cone order; contraction of an edge
discoveries.statement: Let T be a tree of order n with distance matrix D; put ℓ_T(x) = −2^{−(n−2)} det(2xI − D), and for 0 ≤ k ≤ n − 2 let d_k be the coefficient of x^k in ℓ_T (the normalized coefficients of the distance characteristic polynomial; they are positive). For an integer d ≥ 0 let C_d be the set of polynomials Σ_{2e<d} ρ_e x^e (1+x)^{d−2e} + Σ_{d≤2e≤2d} σ_e x^e with real ρ_e, σ_e ≥ 0. S_n is the star of order n. (i) (Statement (Γ_c¹).) Let B be a tree on j ≥ 1 vertices with Laplacian L, c a vertex of B, M = I + x(L + e_c e_cᵀ), and p the vector with p_v = 1 + (2 − deg(v))x for v ≠ c and p_c = 1 + (1 − deg(c))x. Then j(1+x) det M − pᵀ adj(M) p ∈ C_{j+1}. (ii) (Star minimality.) For n ≥ 2: ℓ_T − ℓ_{S_n} ∈ C_{n−1}; in particular d_k(T) ≥ d_k(S_n) for 0 ≤ k ≤ n − 2. (iii) (Lower bound of the peak.) For n ≥ 3 and m = ⌊n/2⌋: d_m(T) − d_{m−1}(T) ≥ d_m(S_n) − d_{m−1}(S_n) > 0, and every index at which the sequence d_0, …, d_{n−2} is maximal is at least ⌊n/2⌋. (iv) (Contraction of an edge.) Let uv be an edge of T neither of whose ends is a leaf, and let T′ be the tree of order n obtained from T by contracting uv and attaching one new pendant vertex at the contracted vertex. Then ℓ_T − ℓ_{T′} ∈ C_{n−1}; in particular d_k(T) ≥ d_k(T′) for 0 ≤ k ≤ n − 2, and d_m(T) − d_{m−1}(T) ≥ d_m(T′) − d_{m−1}(T′) for m = ⌊n/2⌋.

discoveries.title: The generalized tree shift lowers the distance polynomial of a tree in the half-gamma cone order; the path is the coefficientwise maximum
discoveries.statement: Let T be a tree of order n with distance matrix D; put ℓ_T(x) = −2^{−(n−2)} det(2xI − D), and for 0 ≤ k ≤ n − 2 let d_k be the coefficient of x^k in ℓ_T (the normalized coefficients of the distance characteristic polynomial). For an integer d ≥ 0 let C_d be the set of polynomials Σ_{2e<d} ρ_e x^e (1+x)^{d−2e} + Σ_{d≤2e≤2d} σ_e x^e with real ρ_e, σ_e ≥ 0. P_n is the path of order n. (i) (Generalized tree shift.) Let A and B be trees with a ≥ 2 and b ≥ 2 vertices, u a vertex of A, v a vertex of B, and k ≥ 1. Let T_k be the tree obtained from disjoint copies of A and B by joining u to v by a path of length k (with k − 1 new inner vertices), and T′_k the tree obtained by identifying u with v and attaching a new path of length k at the identified vertex; both have order n = a + b + k − 1. Then ℓ_{T_k} − ℓ_{T′_k} ∈ C_{n−1}; in particular d_j(T_k) ≥ d_j(T′_k) for 0 ≤ j ≤ n − 2. (ii) (Path maximality, coefficientwise.) For every tree T of order n ≥ 2: ℓ_{P_n} − ℓ_T ∈ C_{n−1}; in particular d_k(T) ≤ d_k(P_n) for 0 ≤ k ≤ n − 2, and ℓ_T = ℓ_{P_n} only if T is the path. (iii) For n ≥ 3 and 1 ≤ μ ≤ ⌊n/2⌋: d_μ(T) − d_{μ−1}(T) ≤ d_μ(P_n) − d_{μ−1}(P_n). Nothing is asserted about the index at which d_0, …, d_{n−2} is maximal.

discoveries.title: Peak monotonicity under the generalized tree shift, and peak-location maximality of the path
discoveries.statement: For a tree T of order n ≥ 3 let d_0, …, d_{n−2} be the normalized coefficients of its distance characteristic polynomial (the coefficients of ℓ_T(x) = −2^{−(n−2)} det(2xI − D)), and p_max(T) the largest index at which this sequence is maximal. For trees A, B with a, b ≥ 2 vertices, vertices u of A and v of B, and k ≥ 1, let T_k be A and B joined by a path of length k from u to v, and T′_k the tree obtained by identifying u with v and attaching a new path of length k at the identified vertex (Csikvári's generalized tree shift). Conjecture (PM): p_max(T′_k) ≤ p_max(T_k) for all such A, B, u, v, k. Conjecture (PX-peak): p_max(T) ≤ p_max(P_n) for every tree T of order n ≥ 3, P_n the path. (PM) implies (PX-peak); and (PX-peak), together with p_max(P_n) ≤ ⌈n − n/√5⌉, implies the upper bound of the Collins–Shor conjecture (every maximizing index of every tree of order n is at most ⌈n − n/√5⌉).

discoveries.title: The upper bound of the Collins–Shor conjecture for every tree
discoveries.statement: Let T be a tree of order n ≥ 3 with distance matrix D and Laplacian L, let ℓ_T(x) = −2^{−(n−2)} det(2xI − D), and for 0 ≤ k ≤ n − 2 let d_k be the coefficient of x^k in ℓ_T (the normalized coefficients of the distance characteristic polynomial). Then every index p with d_p = max_k d_k satisfies p < n − n/√5 + 3/5; in particular p ≤ ⌈n − n/√5 − 2/5⌉ ≤ ⌈n − n/√5⌉. More precisely, writing the eigenvalues of D/2 as α > 0 > −β_1 ≥ … ≥ −β_{n−1} and q(x) = Π_i (x + β_i): every maximizing index of d_0, …, d_{n−2} is at most every maximizing index of the coefficients of q, and Σ_i 1/(1 + β_i) ≤ n − tr(I + L)^{−1} < n − n/√5 − 2/5.

discoveries.title: The path minimizes the trace of (I + L)^{−1} among trees
discoveries.statement: For every tree T of order n ≥ 1 with Laplacian L, tr (I + L_T)^{−1} ≥ tr (I + L_{P_n})^{−1}, with equality only if T is the path P_n; equivalently, Σ_j μ_j/(1 + μ_j) over the Laplacian eigenvalues of T is maximal exactly for the path. Moreover tr (I + L_{P_n})^{−1} = n/√5 + 2/5 + (2n/√5) r^{2n}/(1 − r^{2n}) with r = φ^{−2}, φ = (1+√5)/2.

discoveries.title: The exact location of the peak of the path, and attainment of the upper bound of Collins–Shor
discoveries.statement: For n ≥ 3 let d_0, …, d_{n−2} be the normalized coefficients of the distance characteristic polynomial of the path P_n, let h_n(k) = 5k³ + 2k² − 4k − 2 − kn², and let k_0(n) be the least integer k ≥ 2 with h_n(k) > 0. Then d_0, …, d_{n−2} is strictly increasing up to the index n − k_0(n) and strictly decreasing after it; so the path has the unique maximizing index p(P_n) = n − k_0(n). Moreover p(P_n) ∈ {⌊n − n/√5⌋, ⌈n − n/√5⌉}; p(P_n) = ⌈n − n/√5⌉ exactly when h_n(⌊n/√5⌋) > 0; this happens only when the fractional part of n/√5 is below 1/5, and it happens whenever that fractional part is below 1/10 and n ≥ 30, hence for infinitely many n.

discoveries.title: Shifted Łukasiewicz t-norms with the drastic boundary: a second (S,N)- and QL-implication among residuals of non-left-continuous t-norms
discoveries.statement: Definitions as in Baczyński–Jayaram (STUDFUZZ 300, 2013; FSS 161, 2010): a t-norm/t-conorm is a commutative, associative operation on [0,1], non-decreasing in each variable, with neutral element 1/0; a fuzzy negation is non-increasing with N(0)=1, N(1)=0; the R-implication of a t-norm T is I_T(x,y)=sup{t in [0,1] : T(x,t) <= y}; an (S,N)-implication is S(N(x),y); a QL-implication is a fuzzy implication of the form S(N(x),T'(x,y)); border-continuity is continuity on [0,1]^2 minus ]0,1[^2; I_WB(x,y)=1 for x<1 and I_WB(1,y)=y. For every real c with 1<c<2 let T_c(x,y)=min(x,y) if max(x,y)=1 and T_c(x,y)=max(0,x+y-c) otherwise. Then T_c is a t-norm that is not border-continuous; its residual is I_c(x,y)=min(1,c-x+y) for x<1 and I_c(1,y)=y; I_c(x,y)=S_L(N_c(x),y)=S_L(N_c(x),min(x,y)) for all x,y in [0,1], where S_L(a,b)=min(1,a+b) and N_c(x)=min(1,c-x) for x<1, N_c(1)=0; I_c(c-1,0)=1, so I_c is not the residual of any left-continuous t-norm; and I_c differs from I_WB and from I_{c'} for c'≠c. Consequently the equality I_{S,N} ∩ (I_T \ I_{T_LC}) = {I_WB} (Problem 4.8.1 of Baczyński–Jayaram 2008, Problem 4.2(i) of their 2013 chapter) fails, and I_WB is not the only QL-implication that is the residual of a non-left-continuous t-norm (Problem 4.5(ii) of the 2013 chapter = Problem 9.4(ii) of the 2010 paper).
